source_name: NBS aktuality – news on opening SIPS/TARGET-SK to non-bank PSPs
why_relevant: Announces that from 6 Oct 2025 PIs and EMIs may apply to participate directly in SIPS or TARGET-SK — a structural change in SK payment-market access, and a leading indicator of new direct participants.

source_name: NBS – Inovačný hub a regulačný sandbox (FinTech innovation facilitators)
why_relevant: NBS's regulatory-dialogue channel for fintech and payments innovation (Inovačný hub since 2019, regulačný sandbox since early 2022), with an annual report on hub/sandbox activity. Reveals NBS's stance on emerging payment business models before any formal rule exists, and which innovation themes are under supervisory examination.

source_name: NBS — Vestník NBS: metodické usmernenia (AML and payment-institution ICS)
why_relevant: The Vestník is the formal publication channel for NBS metodické usmernenia (e.g. MU 3/2019, 4/2019, MU 3/2023; MU 4/2014 on the internal control system of payment institutions and e-money institutions), which set expected AML control standards for banks and PSPs.

source_name: NBS — Európske právo v oblasti poskytovania platobných služieb (NBS working paper/guide)
why_relevant: NBS-published SK-language treatment of EU payment-services law, including the PSD3/PSR proposals and the European Parliament's April 2024 legislative resolution — rare authoritative SK terminology source for the payments legal stack.

source_name: NBS – Príručka pre prípravu žiadosti o udelenie povolenia (licensing application handbook, PDF)
why_relevant: Detailed NBS expectations for PI/EMI licence files (business model, capital, governance, outsourcing). Useful as a proxy for supervisory priorities and for benchmarking entry effort.

source_name: Opatrenie NBS č. 8/2021 o predkladaní výkazov bankami, pobočkami zahraničných bánk a obchodníkmi s CP na štatistické účely (konsolidované znenie)
why_relevant: Core banking statistical reporting measure: enumerates report codes (Cp(NBS)01-12, Mk(NBS)00-12/02-12/03-12/04-12 etc.), periodicity and the 10th-working-day monthly deadline pattern. Consolidated-text PDF is the cleanest machine-parsable calendar for bank statistical returns.

source_name: Opatrenie NBS č. 16/2014 (úplné znenie) – disclosure obligation instrument
why_relevant: The legal instrument that defines what every SK bank must disclose and on what frequency — the schema behind all the Pillar 3 documents above, and the key to knowing when a disclosure is late or missing.

source_name: Opatrenie NBS č. 9/2022 o predkladaní výkazov bankami a obchodníkmi s CP na účely zberu údajov podľa osobitných predpisov
why_relevant: Supervisory-side (not purely statistical) reporting measure for banks — the national hook under which EBA ITS-based FINREP/COREP style data collection is operationalised in SK.

source_name: Opatrenie NBS z 24. marca 2025 o predkladaní výkazov poskytovateľmi služieb kryptoaktív (MiCA reporting)
why_relevant: Newest reporting-obligation layer adjacent to payments (CASPs under MiCA). Signals how NBS extends its return taxonomy to new licence types — a leading indicator of future PSP/EMI reporting changes.

source_name: NBS – Dear CEO letters / supervisory communications to payment service providers
why_relevant: Direct supervisory correspondence addressed to boards of payment-services firms — an unusually candid statement of NBS's supervisory expectations and concerns, of a kind rarely captured in formal legal registers. Found on the legacy www.nbs.sk document tree, which suggests such letters may not be systematically indexed on the new site.

source_name: NBS – Metodika na vypracúvanie hlásenia SLUZ(NBS)1-04 (payment/services reporting methodology PDF)
why_relevant: Concrete per-return methodology document showing the level of detail NBS publishes (codes for payment services, country of origin/destination classification). Template for what to harvest for every return code.

source_name: SLOV-LEX – hromadné pripomienky (mass/collective comments) sub-register
why_relevant: Sub-view of the comment register showing collective/mass comments, which trigger mandatory rozporové konanie (dispute resolution meeting) and therefore predictably delay a measure. High-value early warning that a deadline will move.

source_name: NR SR (Slovak Parliament) document repository – payments bills and explanatory memoranda
why_relevant: Parliamentary texts and dôvodové správy for the payment services act reveal intent, transition periods and derogations that the consolidated law text hides.

source_name: NRSR – parliamentary document preview (tabled supervisory/DPA reports and consumer bills)
why_relevant: The Slovak Parliament hosts tabled versions of the DPA's annual report and of NBS/consumer-protection materials, sometimes with committee positions and dates. A useful mirror when agency sites reorganise, and a place where political pressure on conduct supervision becomes visible.

source_name: Správa z III. kola národného hodnotenia rizík ML/TF (National Risk Assessment, 3rd round)
why_relevant: The NRA sets the risk ratings that drive supervisory intensity and sectoral obligations for banks, payment institutions and VASPs; 3rd round covers 2020-2023. Directly predicts where inspections and new requirements land.

source_name: Národná stratégia boja proti legalizácii výnosov z trestnej činnosti, financovaniu terorizmu a proliferácie (do 2030)
why_relevant: Government-approved AML/CFT/CPF strategy (approved by uznesenie vlády č. 472/2025 per secondary reporting) — forward-looking action plan with owners and deadlines; the best single predictor of upcoming SK AML regulatory workstreams.

source_name: Slovak bank payment-service pages as de-facto implementation evidence (e.g. Slovenská sporiteľňa platobný styk)
why_relevant: Bank product/T&C pages reveal actual go-live dates, limits and cut-off times for instant payments and VOP in SK — the observable end state of scheme rulebook adoption.

source_name: 365.bank group structure page (skupina 365.bank)
why_relevant: Bank-published group structure identifies the legal entities inside the 365.bank / Poštová banka group — the buying units a vendor case study would name, and the entities to match against supplier announcements.

source_name: 365.bank – Obchodné podmienky a sadzobník poplatkov (change series)
why_relevant: 365.bank posts date-stamped T&C and fee-schedule versions (personal-account changes and fee revision effective 1.3.2026; instant-payment limit raised 3k→5k EUR) — concrete evidence of instant-payments regulation landing in retail pricing.

source_name: SK professional-services regulatory trackers (PwC SK, ULC, Avris, Prosman & Pavlovič, Highgate)
why_relevant: Slovak law/advisory firms publish the most explicit SK-language mapping of EU acts to national deadlines and to which SK statute changes (DORA and the 747/2004 amendment, AML package, PSD3/PSR transition periods). Useful for lead-finding and terminology, must be verified against primary sources.

source_name: ČSOB SK – 'Prehľad zmien v podmienkach' / navrhované zmeny VOP notices
why_relevant: ČSOB issues discrete pre-notification documents naming the proposed VOP change and its effective date (e.g. 1.7.2025, 7.10.2025 current-account conditions, accessibility-of-services clause implementing the EU Accessibility Act). Directly maps regulation to contractual deadline.

source_name: ČSOB SK – Informácie zverejňované ročne (Pillar 3, Opatrenie NBS 16/2014)
why_relevant: ČSOB's annual prudential disclosure series with a stable folder id (11005/98584) and date-suffixed filenames — enumerable back-run for capital/risk trend tracking.

source_name: ECB Regulation (EU) 2020/2011 (ECB/2020/59) amending payments statistics Regulation 1409/2013 (ECB/2013/43)
why_relevant: The EU legal basis for PSP payment-statistics reporting (quarterly and semi-annual tables, fraud data) that NBS transposes into its Ps(NBS)/Pb(NBS) returns. Defines the taxonomy and the outer deadline envelope; national deadlines are set by NBS and may be tighter.

source_name: SOI – Výročná správa (annual report)
why_relevant: Annual account of inspection volumes, thematic campaigns, sanctions and ARS caseload; identifies which consumer sectors (incl. credit/leasing/e-commerce payments) were prioritised. Stable /files/documents/kcinnost/{year}/ pattern.

source_name: Chambers Global Practice Guides – Banking Regulation: Slovakia chapter
why_relevant: Annually refreshed, firm-authored English restatement of the Slovak banking regulatory framework (EU law + domestic overlay, NBS as DORA supervisor). Best single structured baseline document written by SK advisers.

source_name: ECB Banking Supervision – List of supervised entities (SI/LSI)
why_relevant: SSM list identifying which SK banks are significant institutions supervised directly by the ECB vs less significant under NBS. Determines which supervisor's consultations and deadlines apply to each SK bank.

source_name: Slovak legal/consumer-finance commentary on new Consumer Credit Act (zákon č. 312/2025 Z. z., CCD2 transposition)
why_relevant: Tracks the single biggest live conduct-regulation change for SK retail banking — the new consumer-credit law transposing CCD2, effective from 2026 — including creditworthiness, disclosure and total-cost rules that drive NBS supervisory priorities and deadlines.

source_name: Podnikajte.sk – practitioner coverage of SK payment obligations (instant payments, VOP)
why_relevant: Business-press explainers translate scheme/EU deadlines into how SK banks actually implement them; useful for detecting divergence between formal deadlines and practice, and for naming banks.

source_name: VÚB banka – Pillar III / Zverejňovanie informácií podľa Opatrenia NBS č. 16/2014
why_relevant: VÚB (Intesa Sanpaolo, O-SII) publishes a highly regular, predictably-named quarterly Pillar 3 PDF series — the cleanest machine-harvestable prudential disclosure set in SK.

source_name: European Commission – merger case files involving SK banks (e.g. M.10378 VUB / Slovenska sporitelna / Tatra banka)
why_relevant: EU merger filings for SK bank joint ventures describe shared infrastructure/service arrangements between the three systemic private banks — evidence of joint procurement and shared-vendor arrangements that no public portal covers.

source_name: Goldmann Systems – Digital finance case studies (365.bank transformation)
why_relevant: Vendor case study naming a named SK bank programme (transformation of digital 365.bank into a full-service bank). Full-service licensing implies regulatory, reporting and product-compliance workstreams — a direct compliance-spend signal for a private bank.

source_name: Highgate.sk — SK law-firm commentary on PSD3/PSR
why_relevant: SK legal/advisory boutiques publish Slovak-language explainers when clients start asking; a cluster of firm posts on one regulation is a weak signal that SK PSPs are entering implementation. Also names the SK-specific licensing consequences (authorisation, transition of existing providers).

entity_name: Law-firm and compliance trackers on Slovak GDPR enforcement
source_name: Law-firm and compliance trackers on Slovak GDPR enforcement (Havel & Partners, Dagital Legal, Podnikajte.sk, i-secure)
why_relevant: Practitioner aggregations of ÚOOÚ fining patterns, fine ceilings and procedural problems of the authority. Useful to reconstruct enforcement trends that the authority itself does not publish case-by-case, and to spot capacity/backlog issues that delay decisions.
